children: A measure of Australian business conditions slid to six-year lows in August as cost pressures squeezed profit margins and firms fretted about the chance of further increases in interest rates, a survey showed on Tuesday.

The survey from National Australia Bank showed its index of business conditions fell five points to -1 in August, the first drop into negative territory since the pandemic hit in 2020. Its index of confidence fell a point to -8, far below the long run average of +5.
The downturn was broad-based across industries, with profitability sinking 10 points and sales five points to reach post-COVID lows.
"The decline in the profitability index bears watching, given its leading relationship with broader labour market conditions," NAB said.
"Overall, the key signals from the survey are slowing growth amid a backdrop of persistence in cost and price pressures."
Measures of costs in the survey remained elevated, with fuel rising in August as the conflict in the Middle East intensified once more.
NAB said the gap between purchase cost growth and product prices was at historically high levels, suggesting businesses faced increasing pressure on margins.
Stubbornly high inflation has sparked speculation the Reserve Bank of Australia will have to lift interest rates for a fourth time this year, perhaps as soon as this month.
